Thanks Marissa — quick answers below.

- Short prompts (~70%): model-driven predictions for batch scoring and embeddings, typically <512 tokens.
- Medium (20%): interactive researcher queries 512–8k tokens.
- Long-context experiments (~10%): large-document retrieval and long-form summarization; of those long runs, maybe 2–3% hit 64k.

Model plan: pilot uses the 7B instruction variant for UI and light throughput. Production intends to use the 70B base (then an instruction-tuned 70B) for higher quality; timeline to flip depends on cost and availability.

Procurement will need an estimate for reserved capacity vs. on-demand for budgeting. If you can highlight the memory delta for the two model families and how quantization (int8 / 4-bit) changes required pods, that would be perfect.

Hi all — attaching a CSV and short notes (attachment: karthik_memory_workup.csv) with the back-of-envelope numbers. Key points summarized here:

1) Baseline model footprints (runtime working set, excludes model weights on CPU/GPU staging):
- 7B (nf4/int8 friendly): ~18–22GB of GPU memory for 8k context at int8-like profiles; peak kv cache add ~6–10GB for 64k segments if requests stream large windows.
- 70B (fp16 baseline): ~58–72GB for 8k context; for 64k context the KV cache multiplier pushes peak working set to ~120–140GB depending on tokenization and attention compilation choices.

2) Quantization impact (typical):
- 4-bit/GPTQ (production safe for 7B, cautiously for 70B): reduces model weight footprint ~2–2.5x vs fp16, but runtime overhead for decoding and custom kernels can increase latency by ~10–20% depending on our kernel choice.
- int8-ish profiles: good middle ground for 70B if you accept small quality delta; reduces memory but often still needs 48–64GB of GPU for comfortable headroom.

3) Pod recommendations (conservative vs flexible):
- Pilot (7B primary, low long-context): 4 x A100-40GB reserved pods with a shared burst pool (adds up to 2x on demand). This covers 100–120 concurrent short QPS with 99th pct latency targets.
- Production (70B inclusive with occasional 64k runs): 6 x A100-80GB or 4 x H100-80GB reserved pods with explicit KV offload policies for the 64k experiments. If you run 70B in fp16 and avoid 64k frequently, a 6-pod pool is fine. If 64k becomes common, we recommend a hybrid: 4 reserved H100 pods + 2 burst H100 instances for experiments.

4) KV cache strategy: prefix caching for recurring document chunks + automatic eviction. If SilverLake can pre-pad / chunk long-doc pipelines to a 32k working set rather than 64k for most experiments, you drop the KV cache multiplier and save ~30–40% GPU memory headroom across the fleet.

5) Expected committed capacity delta vs on-demand: committing to reserved will drop per-token cost ~28–36% depending on utilization and quantization chosen. I included a numeric column-by-column in the CSV.

Action items:
- Catherine: confirm whether you can change the long-doc experiments to a 32k window in the medium term. This is the single biggest lever to reduce committed pod count.
- Marissa/Vanessa: I’ll turn the CSV into the one-page sizing that aligns with finance tables.

Notes on assumptions are at the top of the CSV (batching, typical sequence length, KV eviction policy).
